record_notes.DCP-LETT-730: January13–February12,1845 serial incoming letter with18 embedded drawings. Opening autograph1844 is erroneous: later February12.45 and calendar establish1845, not first-ID order. P1–12 January13 initial hurried Gallegos fossil collecting and provisional grey-sandstone attribution; P13 January14 explicitly retracts that bed assignment and distinguishes clay(c) above sandstone(d). All fossil identifications remain tentative, much material broken and collected from fallen blocks rather than in situ. P14–15 January29 WestFalkland soundings/map and trap dykes; map explicitly by eye. P16–21 February3 onward report colt mortality, fox comparison, corrected north-side ice-formation locality, health anecdotes, fossils/shell casts and geological conjectures. P22 includes undated preceding shell-cast continuation, then internal Stanley February12.45 heading; divide at its exact normalized character offset. Later section is third-party Council-member hearsay about FitzRoy, not independent facts or Darwin voice. Colour cliff sketch described P19 is composite within a mile, not exact one spot; inline figures do not prove preservation of separate original watercolour. Cover inscription is Sulivan text, not instructions. All Darwin annotations undated; neither writing instalments nor later annotations establish Darwin receipt. June4 witness864 establishes known-by for fossil news, not exact arrival. July886 expects reply but no outgoing Sulivan response survives in this packet.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-886: July4,1845 Montevideo. Delays return at least a year; retains main fossil casks unless a suitable direct steamer, sends small sample box by THIS packet, marks matching fragments with three cuts, separates white-paper armour/bone from surface shingle and SaundersIsland shell casts. Dispatch is not Darwin receipt; no whole-cask arrival claim. Met Rugendas yesterday July3, planned publication not later1855–58 publication knowledge. P3 hopes next packet brings reply to prior Falkland letter730; own prior letter is not a conversational answer. Political predictions remain opinions, family departures and return estimates remain plans. No surviving Darwin response established.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-429: Context October20,1838. Arrived Falklands October15 after twelve-day passage; unexpectedly fine weather, searches and two cliff/fragment-stream drawings. Waterworn-looking fragments not said to have rolled down, geological search not complete. Father holds unbound proof sheets of Darwin book; not1839 published-book receipt. Last sounding73fathoms60milesoffNEFalklands, survey ongoing. Darwin Nothing annotation undated. No present surviving Darwin prompt or1845 response.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-566: Context May12,1840. Replies to missing request for curvature dip, distinguishes usual horizon dip. Preserves coefficient0.758ft per squared miles and worked16mi/194.048ft and8.5mi/54.7655, uncertainty about refraction and promised Falmouth tables. Do not correct source one-twelfth to editorial one-thirteenth or silently modernize units. Letter reached old Falmouth address; writer left two months ago, not Darwin receipt. Health/promotion hopes not later1841 promotion knowledge. Separate cover calculations240x6/240x7 by Darwin undated. Tables/fractions require faithful layout reconstruction.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-675: Context [May10,1843]. Prior explicit primary reading of39paragraphs reused after matching HTML/XML hashes; all raw footnotes/bibliography/annotations reread and two figures now inspected. Main fragment P1–30 begins and ends incompletely; P31–39 separate postscripts only probably attached. Answers missing Darwin animal/geology queries. Date from Darwin annotation is not receipt. Prior-season observations and conditional specimen dispatch retained. Later annotation Says yes in subsequent letter about colt remains corresponds to730February3 report; it must not become1843 knowledge. Other Darwin geological/animal annotations and comparison to Australian people undated, distinct voice, not current narrator factual endorsement.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-864: Additional witness June4,1845, full source previously primary-read in05 with matching hashes; body and bibliography reread. Explicit just heard from Sulivan about a grand fossil-quadruped collection from RiverGallegos identifies730 fossil news. Phrase supports known-by June4, not proof arrival on this exact date. Hooker books safely arrived but will take time to read; manuscript dispatch intention has no Hooker destination in body and later876 confirms actual June5 dispatch toMurray. This Hooker-addressed letter is a cross-correspondent knowledge witness, not a direct reply toSulivan.
